title: ～ようと思う (〜you to omou)
shortExplanation: Expresses the speaker's intention or plan to do something.
longExplanation: The ～ようと思う grammar point is used to express the speaker's intention or plan to do something in the future. It can be translated as 'I think I will...' or 'I am planning to...' in English. It is formed by taking the volitional form of a verb and adding と思う.

examples.jp: 今日は早く寝ようと思います。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa hayaku neyou to omoimasu.
examples.en: I think I will go to bed early today.

examples.jp: 明日美術館に行こうと思っています。
examples.romaji: Ashita bijutsukan ni ikou to omotteimasu.
examples.en: I am planning to go to the art museum tomorrow.

examples.jp: 新しいカメラを買おうと思います。
examples.romaji: Atarashii kamera wo kaou to omoimasu.
examples.en: I think I will buy a new camera.

examples.jp: 来週友達と映画を見ようと思っています。
examples.romaji: Raishuu tomodachi to eiga wo miyou to omotteimasu.
examples.en: I am planning to watch a movie with my friend next week.

usageNote: "I think I will.../I plan to". (Near-duplicate of n4-058 - same construction, taught at both N3 and N4.)
